items.title: Steam Frame Making Use Of Zink For OpenGL On Vulkan
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Valve's Steam Frame VR headset that makes use of a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 SoC with Adreno graphics is using the open-source "Turnip" Vulkan driver from Mesa as reported last year. For OpenGL it turns out that the Mesa Zink driver is being used on the Steam Frame for OpenGL atop the Vulkan API...</article>

items.title: Google's "Painful To Maintain" Binder C Linux Driver Being Removed In Favor Of Rust
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Google's Binder driver written in the C programming language has long been part of the mainline kernel as the inter-process communication (IPC) mechanism used on Android. The past few years the Binder driver was rewritten in Rust as one of the first "real" drivers in the Rust programming language. The Rust Binder driver was upstreamed in Linux 6.18 and now for the upcoming Linux 7.4 kernel cycle, the old Binder C-based driver is set to be retired...</article>

items.title: AMD Strix Halo Enjoys Some Performance Gains On Ubuntu 26.10, Especially With amd64v3
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Ahead of next week's Ubuntu 26.10 beta release I have been testing the "Stonking Stingray" on a variety of systems. Ubuntu 26.10 is performing well overall with some nice upgrades over Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, especially if opting to use the new snapshot/daily ISOs of Ubuntu 26.10 in amd64v3 form for x86_64-v3 packages. In today's tests are a look at the performance benefits of Ubuntu 26.10 on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ "Strix Halo".</article>

items.title: Linux Ready With Fix For Intel's FRED Crashing Some Games Under Wine / Steam Play
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Recently there have been some bug reports to Mesa around Intel Panther Lake graphics crashing with some games like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Elden Ring crashing or freezing quite quickly. This turns out not to be an Intel Xe3 Arc Graphics B390 driver bug with Panther Lake but rather due to a kernel issue with the new Flexible and Return Event Delivery "FRED" that debuted with the Core Ultra Series 3 processors...</article>

items.title: Linux Kernel Build Times Ready To Be Significantly Reduced With Latest Patches
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The past few weeks we have eagerly been following a Linux kernel patch series after AI found some major bottlenecks in the Linux kernel build code. With AI helping to address these bottlenecks, Linux kernel build times are substantially reduced. These optimizations might be ready in time for Linux 7.4 for reducing incremental kernel build times as much as around 70%. This week the latest iteration of these patches were posted by Arm engineer Lorenzo Stoakes...</article>

This week another round of AMDGPU kernel graphics driver updates were sent out ahead of the Linux 7.4 merge window in October...</article>
